quotes.text: Delegated permissions come into play when an actual user is signed in and using your app. You're piggybacking off their identity, working in the bubble of what they're already allowed to see and do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A plain-language definition of delegated permissions.

quotes.text: If compromised, a single poorly planned app could read sensitive emails, HR data or customer info across the tenant without anyone noticing. That explains why the admin roadblock exists. It's a fail safe, not an obstacle.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes admin consent as a safeguard rather than a blocker.

quotes.text: That's where the principle of least privilege kicks in. An old idea, but the best trick for smooth graph deployments only ask for what your app actually needs, not what you might want later.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable recommendation for scoping Graph permissions.

quotes.text: Build your app with the flexibility to request scopes as late as possible based on what the user actually tries to do. That approach not only simplifies consent, but keeps your risk visibility low.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical design advice for requesting permissions incrementally.

quotes.text: Before you cut a single line of code, sketch out exactly which permissions your app needs and review it with whoever controls consent in your tenant.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode in one concrete planning step.

chapters.title: Why Graph API access breaks in production
Consent confusion: why some permissions demand admins
What it all boils down to

takeaways: Apps that work in a permissive dev tenant often fail in production because enterprise consent policies restrict which Graph permissions users can grant.
Delegated permissions act within a signed-in user's rights, while application permissions let an app act on its own across the organization and therefore require admin consent.
Requesting only the narrowest scopes, piloting with trusted users and preparing admin approval early keeps Graph-based rollouts on track.
hook: Your Graph-powered app passes every test, then hits a wall of admin approval prompts in production. This episode is for developers, makers and admins who build or approve apps on Microsoft Graph. You will learn how delegated and application permissions differ, why some need admin consent, and how least privilege keeps rollouts smooth.
